## Question 1

For a positive integer $n$, let &nbsp;$P$: $n$ is odd &nbsp;&nbsp;and&nbsp;&nbsp; $Q$: $n^{2}\equiv1\pmod{16}$.

Which one of the following is true?

&nbsp;&nbsp;**A** $P$ is sufficient but not necessary for $Q$ &nbsp;&nbsp;**B** $P$ is necessary but not sufficient for $Q$

&nbsp;&nbsp;**C** $P$ is necessary and sufficient for $Q$ &nbsp;&nbsp;**D** $P$ is neither necessary nor sufficient for $Q$

---

## Question 2

Both roots of $x^{2}+bx+c=0$ are real and lie strictly between $0$ and $1$. Which one of the following is
**not** a necessary consequence?

&nbsp;&nbsp;**A** $c>0$ &nbsp;&nbsp;**B** $-2<b<0$ &nbsp;&nbsp;**C** $1+b+c>0$ &nbsp;&nbsp;
**D** $b^{2}\ge4c$ &nbsp;&nbsp;**E** $c<\tfrac14$

---

## Question 3

A sequence $(a_n)$ is said to converge to $L$ if

$$\forall\varepsilon>0\ \ \exists N\ \ \forall n>N:\quad \lvert a_n-L\rvert<\varepsilon .$$

Which one of the following says that $(a_n)$ does **not** converge to $L$?

&nbsp;&nbsp;**A** $\forall\varepsilon>0\ \exists N\ \forall n>N:\ \lvert a_n-L\rvert\ge\varepsilon$

&nbsp;&nbsp;**B** $\exists\varepsilon>0\ \forall N\ \exists n>N:\ \lvert a_n-L\rvert\ge\varepsilon$

&nbsp;&nbsp;**C** $\exists\varepsilon>0\ \exists N\ \forall n>N:\ \lvert a_n-L\rvert\ge\varepsilon$

&nbsp;&nbsp;**D** $\forall\varepsilon>0\ \forall N\ \exists n>N:\ \lvert a_n-L\rvert\ge\varepsilon$

&nbsp;&nbsp;**E** $\exists\varepsilon>0\ \forall N\ \forall n>N:\ \lvert a_n-L\rvert\ge\varepsilon$

---

## Question 4

All variables below are real. Which of the following statements are **true**?

&nbsp;&nbsp;**1** $\forall x\ \exists y\ \forall z:\ x+y>z$ &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
**2** $\exists y\ \forall x:\ x+y>x$

&nbsp;&nbsp;**3** $\forall x\ \forall y\ \exists z:\ z>x+y$ &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
**4** $\exists x\ \forall y:\ xy=0$

&nbsp;&nbsp;**A** 2 only &nbsp;&nbsp;**B** 2 and 3 only &nbsp;&nbsp;**C** 2, 3 and 4 only
&nbsp;&nbsp;**D** 1, 2 and 3 only &nbsp;&nbsp;**E** all four

---

## Question 5

Let $m\ge2$ be an integer and let $k\ge2$ be an integer. Consider

&nbsp;&nbsp;$(*)$ &nbsp; for every positive integer $n$: if $m$ divides $n^{k}$ then $m$ divides $n$.

Which one of the following describes exactly the $m$ for which $(*)$ holds for **every** $k\ge2$?

&nbsp;&nbsp;**A** $m$ is prime &nbsp;&nbsp;**B** $m$ is a product of distinct primes
&nbsp;&nbsp;**C** $m$ is not a perfect power

&nbsp;&nbsp;**D** $m$ is odd &nbsp;&nbsp;**E** every $m\ge2$

---

## Question 6

Consider the statement:

&nbsp;&nbsp;$(*)$ &nbsp; $n^{2}+n+41$ is prime for every integer $n\ge0$.

The statement is false. What is the **smallest** $n\ge0$ for which it fails, and why?

&nbsp;&nbsp;**A** $n=40$, because the value is then $41^{2}$

&nbsp;&nbsp;**B** $n=41$, because every term is then a multiple of $41$

&nbsp;&nbsp;**C** $n=40$, because the value is then $40\times41$

&nbsp;&nbsp;**D** $n=43$, because the value is then divisible by $43$

&nbsp;&nbsp;**E** $n=1$, because $43$ is not prime

---

## Question 7

A student argues:

> Since $\lvert x-3\rvert<1$, we have $2<x<4$. &nbsp;**(1)**
> Hence $x-2>0$, so multiplying $\dfrac{1}{x-2}<1$ by $x-2$ gives $1<x-2$. &nbsp;**(2)**
> Therefore $x>3$. &nbsp;**(3)**
> So the solution set of $\dfrac{1}{x-2}<1$ is $x>3$. &nbsp;**(4)**

Which one of the following is correct?

&nbsp;&nbsp;**A** The argument is valid and the conclusion is correct.

&nbsp;&nbsp;**B** Step (1) is wrong.

&nbsp;&nbsp;**C** Step (2) is wrong, because $x-2$ could be negative.

&nbsp;&nbsp;**D** Steps (1)–(3) are valid, but (4) is wrong: they used an extra assumption not in the
original inequality.

&nbsp;&nbsp;**E** Step (3) is wrong.

---

## Question 8

A student is asked to solve $x^{3}=x$ and writes:

| | |
|---|---|
| Step 1 | $x^{3}-x=0$ |
| Step 2 | $x\left(x^{2}-1\right)=0$ |
| Step 3 | Dividing by $x$: $x^{2}-1=0$ |
| Step 4 | $x=1$ or $x=-1$ |

Which one of the following is true?

&nbsp;&nbsp;**A** The first error is in Step 1 &nbsp;&nbsp;**B** The first error is in Step 2
&nbsp;&nbsp;**C** The first error is in Step 3

&nbsp;&nbsp;**D** The first error is in Step 4 &nbsp;&nbsp;**E** There is no error

---

## Question 9

The real numbers $a,b,c,d$ are all greater than $1$ and satisfy $\log_c d=\left(\log_a b\right)^{3}$. Use some
of the lines below to construct a proof that $\log_b d=\left(\log_a b\right)^{2}\left(\log_a c\right)$.

&nbsp;&nbsp;**(1)** Let $x=\log_a b$, $y=\log_a c$ &nbsp;&nbsp;**(2)** $d=c^{\left(x^{3}\right)}$
&nbsp;&nbsp;**(3)** $d=b^{\left(x^{2}y\right)}$ &nbsp;&nbsp;**(4)** $d=\left(a^{y}\right)^{\left(x^{3}\right)}$

&nbsp;&nbsp;**(5)** $d=a^{\left(x^{3}y\right)}$ &nbsp;&nbsp;**(6)** $d=\left(a^{x}\right)^{\left(x^{2}y\right)}$

&nbsp;&nbsp;**A** (1), (3), (6), (5), (4), (2) &nbsp;&nbsp;**B** (1), (2), (4), (5), (6), (3)
&nbsp;&nbsp;**C** (1), (2), (5), (4), (6), (3)

&nbsp;&nbsp;**D** (1), (4), (2), (5), (6), (3) &nbsp;&nbsp;**E** (1), (3), (5), (4), (2), (6)

---

## Question 10

Consider the statement about integers $n$:

&nbsp;&nbsp;$(*)$ &nbsp; if $n$ is prime and $n>2$, then $n$ is odd.

Which one of the following is the **contrapositive** of $(*)$?

&nbsp;&nbsp;**A** If $n$ is even then $n$ is not prime and $n\le2$.

&nbsp;&nbsp;**B** If $n$ is even then $n$ is not prime or $n\le2$.

&nbsp;&nbsp;**C** If $n$ is odd then $n$ is prime and $n>2$.

&nbsp;&nbsp;**D** If $n$ is not prime or $n\le2$ then $n$ is even.

&nbsp;&nbsp;**E** If $n$ is even then $n$ is prime and $n>2$.

---

&nbsp;&nbsp;**A** $n^{2}\equiv0\pmod 8$ &nbsp;&nbsp;**B** $n^{2}\equiv4\pmod 8$
&nbsp;&nbsp;**C** $n^{2}\equiv1\pmod 8$

&nbsp;&nbsp;**D** $n^{2}\equiv5\pmod 8$ &nbsp;&nbsp;**E** $n^{3}\equiv5\pmod 8$

## Question 12

The positive integers $a$ and $b$ satisfy $\gcd(a,b)=6$ and $\operatorname{lcm}(a,b)=180$. How many
**ordered pairs** $(a,b)$ are there?

&nbsp;&nbsp;**A** $1$ &nbsp;&nbsp;**B** $2$ &nbsp;&nbsp;**C** $4$ &nbsp;&nbsp;**D** $6$ &nbsp;&nbsp;**E** $8$

## Question 13

The numbers $1,2,\dots,10$ are written on a board. A **move** consists of rubbing out two numbers $a$ and $b$
and writing $a+b-1$ in their place. Moves are repeated until one number remains.

Which one of the following is true?

&nbsp;&nbsp;**A** The final number depends on the order of the moves.

&nbsp;&nbsp;**B** The final number is always $55$. &nbsp;&nbsp;**C** The final number is always $46$.

&nbsp;&nbsp;**D** The final number is always $45$. &nbsp;&nbsp;**E** The process never terminates.

---

## Question 14

Let $x$ be real and let $T$ be the set with $\lvert x-1\rvert<2$. Which one of the following is a condition
that is **necessary and sufficient** for $x\in T$?

&nbsp;&nbsp;**A** $0<x<4$ &nbsp;&nbsp;**B** $x^{2}-2x-3<0$ &nbsp;&nbsp;**C** $x^{3}<27$
&nbsp;&nbsp;**D** $\lvert x\rvert<3$ &nbsp;&nbsp;**E** $x<3$

---

## Question 15

$ABCD$ is a convex quadrilateral whose diagonals are **equal in length and perpendicular**. Let $E,F,G,H$ be
the midpoints of $AB,BC,CD,DA$. Which one of the following must be true?

&nbsp;&nbsp;**A** $ABCD$ is a square &nbsp;&nbsp;**B** $ABCD$ is a rhombus &nbsp;&nbsp;
**C** $EFGH$ is a square

&nbsp;&nbsp;**D** $EFGH$ is a rhombus but not a square &nbsp;&nbsp;**E** $EFGH$ is a rectangle but not a square

## Question 16

How many $3$-element subsets of $\{1,2,\dots,9\}$ have the property that **every pair** of their elements is
coprime?

&nbsp;&nbsp;**A** $29$ &nbsp;&nbsp;**B** $33$ &nbsp;&nbsp;**C** $37$ &nbsp;&nbsp;**D** $41$
&nbsp;&nbsp;**E** $45$

## Question 17

Let $P$ and $Q$ be statements about a real number $x$. It is known that

&nbsp;&nbsp;• "$P$ or $Q$" is true for every $x$, and &nbsp;• "$P$ and $Q$" is false for every $x$.

Which one of the following must be true?

&nbsp;&nbsp;**A** $P$ is true for every $x$ &nbsp;&nbsp;**B** $Q$ is the negation of $P$
&nbsp;&nbsp;**C** $P\Rightarrow Q$ for every $x$

&nbsp;&nbsp;**D** $P$ is false for every $x$ &nbsp;&nbsp;**E** nothing can be deduced

---

## Question 18

Consider this attempted proof that $\sqrt2$ is irrational.

> Suppose $\sqrt2=\dfrac pq$ in lowest terms. &nbsp;**(1)**
> Then $p^{2}=2q^{2}$, so $p^{2}$ is even. &nbsp;**(2)**
> Hence $p$ is even, say $p=2r$. &nbsp;**(3)**
> Then $4r^{2}=2q^{2}$, so $q^{2}=2r^{2}$ and $q$ is even. &nbsp;**(4)**
> So $p$ and $q$ are both even, contradicting lowest terms. &nbsp;**(5)**

Which step uses a fact that itself requires proof, and which fact is it?

&nbsp;&nbsp;**A** (2) — that a square of an even number is even

&nbsp;&nbsp;**B** (3) — that $p^{2}$ even implies $p$ even

&nbsp;&nbsp;**C** (4) — that $4r^{2}=2q^{2}$ implies $q^{2}=2r^{2}$

&nbsp;&nbsp;**D** (5) — that a fraction can be written in lowest terms

&nbsp;&nbsp;**E** none — every step is immediate

---

&nbsp;&nbsp;**A** $0$ &nbsp;&nbsp;**B** $14$ &nbsp;&nbsp;**C** $28$ &nbsp;&nbsp;**D** $29$
&nbsp;&nbsp;**E** $33$

## Question 20

Let $S$ be a set of statements about an integer $n$, and suppose that for statements $X,Y$ in $S$ we write
$X\to Y$ to mean "$X\Rightarrow Y$ is true". Suppose

$$A\to B,\qquad B\to C,\qquad C\to A,\qquad A\to D .$$

Which one of the following must be true?

&nbsp;&nbsp;**A** $D\to A$ &nbsp;&nbsp;**B** $B$ and $C$ are equivalent, and both imply $D$

&nbsp;&nbsp;**C** $D$ and $A$ are equivalent &nbsp;&nbsp;**D** $B\to D$ but $C\not\to D$

&nbsp;&nbsp;**E** nothing further can be deduced

:::
